correctness.rationale: The normalized-weight reduction is exhaustive: dominant coordinate yields the correct iff equality; otherwise all six weights are below p and p>1/6. The interval (1/6,1/5] forces all pairs to win; [1/5,1/4] uses disjoint-losing-edge exclusion, at least ten winning pairs, all winning triples; [1/4,1/3] uses perfect-matching coverage to force >=5 winning pairs, an injection of losing triples into winning-pair triangles, and triangle bound t<=2k-8 for all 6-vertex graphs. Each case yields a strictly positive p-polynomial gap, independently established analytically and by exact rational Bernstein certificates. A standalone Python checker exhausts all 32768 graph masks, not merely samples. Conclusions hold for every real p and real weights in the stated ranges; no claim for m>6.

The structural graph argument combines perfect-matching and triangle constraints to control the first overlapping subset sizes; it is not a routine substitution, known-table recomputation, or isolated arbitrary numerical slice.
